Mushrooms, Tomatoes and Spinach Fry-Up

British · Easy · Serves 2

- **Three clocks, one pan, strict order:** mushrooms 6 minutes alone, tomatoes 5 beside them, spinach 90 seconds at the end. Reversing any pair undercooks one and waters the other. - **The mushrooms' dry start:** no butter yet — a drop of oil and a hot pan, cut-faces down, until they brown before the butter arrives. Buttered from the start, they poach grey in their own water. - The spinach washed and dripping slightly — its clinging water is all the wilt it needs.

Mushrooms, Tomatoes and Spinach Fry-Up

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 30 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The vegetables

  • 250 g chestnut mushrooms, halved or thickly sliced
  • 3 medium vine tomatoes (350 g), halved through the equator
  • 200 g baby spinach

The pan's fat and seasoning

  • 30 g butter, divided
  • 15 ml / 14 g olive oil
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 1 tsp (2 g) brown sugar, for the tomatoes
  • 0.5 g grated nutmeg — the spinach's classic partner
  • 2 garlic cloves, sliced (optional — the garden plate's one indulgence)

The plate's anchors

  • 2 large eggs (110 g)
  • 2 thick slices (140 g) bread, fried in the pan's butter
  • Brown breakfast sauce or mushroom ketchup — the latter earns its place here

Instructions

  1. **Mushrooms dry-brown, 6 minutes.** Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and lay the mushrooms cut-faces down, undisturbed 3 minutes to chestnut colour. Toss once, give 2–3 minutes more, then add half the butter, the garlic if using, and a third of the salt — tossing until glossy. Checkpoint — mushrooms browned and glossed, pan dry of liquid, no grey watery phase ever seen. This is the plate's savoury base.
  2. **Tomatoes in, cut-face up, 5 minutes.** Push the mushrooms to the pan's edge and sit the tomato halves cut-face up in the hot centre with the sugar, a grain of salt each, and a drop of the pan's butter. Cook 5 minutes until slumped and jammy, spooning the pan's butter over them once or twice. Checkpoint — tomatoes collapsed by a quarter, their cavities reduced to bubbling glaze; the mushrooms beside them have taken on the tomato's perfume — the pan's own vinaigrette forming.
  3. **The fried bread in butter, 3 minutes.** Lift the vegetables to warm plates. The last of the butter into the pan, and the bread fried 90 seconds a side to golden. Checkpoint — bread golden, crust-edged, butter-drunk — the plate's starch and structure.
  4. **Spinach's 90 seconds, then the eggs.** The spinach into the pan's remaining butter over medium heat, tossed constantly 60–90 seconds to wilted gloss; nutmeg, salt, and pepper over; lift beside the tomatoes. Then the eggs cracked into the pan's last butter, basted 2 minutes to set whites and running yolks. Checkpoint — spinach glossy and just-wilted, still green, seasoned with its nutmeg; eggs lace-edged with liquid yolks — the plate's sauce, as ever.
  5. **Plate the garden fry-up.** Fried bread at the base, eggs at the crown, mushrooms and tomatoes flanking, spinach in its glossy mound, sauce at the side. Checkpoint — the eating test: yolk over the bread, mushroom through the sauce, tomato's acid and spinach's green between — the fry-up's rhythm, entirely vegetable, entirely serious.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Everything watery on the plateWet mushrooms, crowded pan, or spinach overwiltedDry brown first; one layer; 90 seconds' wilt
Tomatoes raw-tastingCut-face down frying instead of upCut-face up, in the pan's centre heat, the full 5 minutes
Spinach grey and sludgyOvercooked or salted earlyLast-in, fast-out; salt and nutmeg at the lift
Plate felt insubstantialNo egg or no fried breadThe two anchors are the plate's architecture — keep both

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Mushrooms and tomatoes batch and reheat** (3 days) beautifully; spinach and eggs are always à la minute. The plate assembles in 10 minutes from a batched base. - **Variation — the vegan garden plate:** olive oil for butter, the tofu scramble for eggs, and the shiitake bacon's crunch on top — the vegan master's greenest hour. - **Variation — the supper direction:** the same pan over pasta — the vegetables and their butter tossed through tagliatelle, the egg becoming the sauce's emulsifier. The fry-up's techniques, repurposed at eight in the evening. - **On the canon:** this plate, the vegetarian master, and the vegan master are the meatless trilogy — one for the vegetables-first, one for the haloumi-hearted, one for the plant-committed.
